blocks.x: Located less than three hours from Penn Station, the highly walkable, historic city of Lancaster, PA has been dubbed the “new Brooklyn” by the NY Post for its booming food scene. And if you’ve been dreaming of a fall getaway from New York City without renting a car, this is the day trip you need to plan.
While NYC has its share of incredible greenmarkets, a trip to Lancaster offers the ultimate combination: crisp autumn air, authentic Pennsylvania Dutch food, and remarkable architecture.

Lancaster Central Market traces its roots all the way back to 1730. Today, it remains the oldest continuously operating farmers market in the U.S., drawing foodies and history buffs alike to its stunning 1889 red-brick Romanesque Revival building right in the center of town.

Best of all, planning a getaway right now lines up perfectly with what experts predict will be a “long, spectacular” fall foliage season across the East Coast—giving you front-row seats to peak autumn colors along the journey.
Here’s how to plan the perfect foodie weekend surrounded by Pennsylvania’s breathtaking autumn scenery.

Source / Lancaster Central Market
What you can actually eat
Lancaster Central Market isn’t your average neighborhood produce stand. It’s a permanent, indoor fixture housing over 60 vendors that reflect the region’s rich agricultural history.
The vendor lineup is completely stacked with Pennsylvania Dutch treats, fresh harvest produce, and handcrafted goods that are incredibly hard to find outside of Amish country.

According to market history, visitors can expect a massive variety of fresh regional bounty. We’re talking about hardwood smoked hams and bacon from S. Clyde Weaver, farm-fresh produce from the Stoner Family Vegetable stand (who have been selling there for over 100 years!), and fresh-ground roots from Long’s Horseradish.
Beyond the fresh produce and meats, you can also stock up on authentic Amish specialties like wet-bottom shoofly pie and whoopie pies, Pennsylvania Dutch sausage, and scrapple.
And because the market has evolved with the city, you’ll also find an incredible array of international cuisine, from authentic Puerto Rican empanadas to fresh Slavic and Middle Eastern fare.

Source / Lancaster Central Market
Fall 2026 Market Events You Can’t Miss
While the authentic Pennsylvania Dutch food and historic architecture are enough of a draw on their own, the market is also a vibrant hub of community entertainment.
If you’re planning a trip before the end of 2026, time your visit to coincide with one of these major upcoming events:

Harvest Breakfast (Saturday, October 3, 2026): From 8 am to 12 pm, the market transforms for one of its most delicious and fun mornings of the year. Expect special harvest-themed, pay-per-stand foods, live music, face painting, and pumpkin painting

ExtraGive (Friday, November 20, 2026): If you visit the weekend before Thanksgiving, you’ll catch the market participating in Lancaster’s massive county-wide giving day, which always features unique activities and community fun

Mayor’s Tree Lighting (Friday, November 27, 2026): Spending the holiday weekend in town? A select group of vendors keep the market open late (from 5 pm to 8 pm) so you can shop under the evening lights, grab warm drinks, and enjoy the magical holiday atmosphere

Even if you visit on a regular shopping day, you’ll step right out of the market doors into downtown Lancaster’s bustling city center, which is packed with local theaters, galleries, and seasonal street festivals to round out your weekend.

Source / Lancaster Central Market
What to know and how to get there
Before you pack your bags for this Amish country fall getaway, there’s one major local quirk to plan around: The market is only open three days a week.
You can only shop on Tuesdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from 6 am to 3 pm. Get there early to beat the weekend crowds and secure the best baked goods before they sell out.
You also don’t need a car to get your small-town fix. The easiest and most relaxing way to arrive is via Amtrak’s Keystone Service.

You can catch the train at Moynihan Train Hall at Penn Station for a relaxing ride that takes just under 3 hours (averaging around 2 hours and 50 minutes). The train drops you directly at Lancaster Station, just a short walk or quick rideshare away from the heart of downtown and the historic Market Square.
If you book your tickets in advance, one-way fares often start at just $33.
Pro tip: The journey takes you straight through the Pennsylvania countryside, offering fantastic fall foliage views right from your window–so be sure to keep your eyes peeled!
